scope: Isolated S1 containment of a child frame's failure to that frame. The experimental patch keeps a view's document and scope when its own top-level document and pending top-level navigation did not run in the failed event loop, and navigates each failed child frame of that view to Servo's error page through its parent. Twelve frame cases now assert this behavior: four shared and eight multiprocess-only. The same-site pending frame cases and the cross-site navigation parse cases keep their assertions, because the failed event loop ran the view's own top-level document. No product dependency or runtime configuration changes.
owner_decisions: A child frame's failure must stay inside that frame. A healthy parent in another event loop keeps its document and its scope, and only the failed frame shows an error state. This applies to an active frame and to a frame whose navigation is pending (2026-11-26).
A view whose own top-level document ran in the failed event loop has failed itself. It receives revocation and its own error state (2026-11-26).
A failed pending top-level navigation replaces the healthy active document with an error page (2026-11-24).

configuration.crash_page_check: Each fetched crash document must contain the engine's failure reason. Servo's crash.html embeds that reason. The check only orders the fixture and grants no host authority.
configuration.containment_check: Each converted case holds the healthy parent's script thread at a barrier and queues eight mixed scoped and unscoped callbacks there. Inside the barrier, the host waits until the frame state probe shows that the failed pipeline is gone, and for a pending navigation that the old child pipeline is still current and live with no pending pipeline. It also waits for revocation of each other view in the failed event loop and then for 200 milliseconds. A revocation or crash notification of the parent also ends the wait, so the next check reports it. The parent must then have no terminal callback, no revocation, and no crash notification. After release, all eight callbacks must succeed in the parent's document. The frame state probe must then report a new, live frame pipeline whose crash details begin with the exact reason and no pending pipeline.
configuration.frame_state_probe: frame_state_for_document_scope_probe reads the constellation's record of the active top-level document's newest child frame: its current pipeline, whether that pipeline is live, its load data's crash details, and whether the frame has a pending pipeline. Page JavaScript cannot supply these values.

engine_patch.change: handle_panic now sorts the views with a pipeline in the failed event loop. top_level_failed holds for a view without a top-level browsing context, or whose active top-level pipeline or a pending top-level pipeline ran in the failed event loop. Those views keep the existing handle_panic_in_webview recovery. For every other view, contained_failed_frames finds each outermost child browsing context whose current or pending pipeline ran in the failed event loop and builds a crash load from that pipeline's load data with every sandboxing flag. It closes any other pending pipeline of that frame and marks inactive history pipelines in the failed event loop for reload. After the failed pipelines close, the constellation sends the existing NavigateIframe message with history replacement to the frame's parent pipeline, so the parent's frame element accepts the crash pipeline as its own navigation. In script_thread.rs, pre_page_load sends a child frame's crash load through the fetch path instead of the synchronous about:blank, about:srcdoc, and javascript: URL paths. Top-level crash loads are unchanged. Probe instrumentation: FrameStateForDocumentScopeProbe and WebView::frame_state_for_document_scope_probe report the newest child frame's current pipeline, liveness, crash details, and pending state.

changes.name: A child frame's failure replaced the whole view
changes.observed: Before this change, the panic handler and the lifeline handler revoked and replaced every view with a pipeline in the failed event loop, including a healthy parent whose only failed pipeline was a child frame's active or pending pipeline.
changes.fix: The panic handler now revokes and recovers only views whose own top-level document or pending top-level navigation ran in the failed event loop. Every other view keeps its document and scope, and each failed child frame navigates to Servo's error page through its parent. Twelve converted cases check this, and the first negative control fails at the first converted case.

changes.name: A srcdoc frame's crash load would render its markup again
changes.observed: Servo loads about:srcdoc, about:blank, and javascript: URL documents synchronously and ignores the crash details. A sandboxed srcdoc frame's crash load parsed the srcdoc markup again and requested its withheld script a second time.
changes.fix: A child frame's crash load now always uses the fetch path, so it shows Servo's error page. The third negative control fails at the sandboxed srcdoc case without this change.

changes.name: Lone pending frame pipelines depend on the lifeline's pending-change clause
changes.observed: No negative control isolated this clause for frames before this checkpoint.
changes.fix: None. The second negative control restricts the clause to top-level pipelines and fails at the first lone pending frame process case.

findings: In every converted case, the healthy parent has no terminal callback, no revocation, and no crash notification while its script thread is held after the failure. All eight held callbacks then succeed in the parent's document, and its retained reply passes the host allocation check.

The failed frame gets a new, live pipeline whose crash details begin with the exact reason, and no pending pipeline remains. The parent still receives SecurityError when it reads the frame, because the error page has an opaque origin. In the pending cases, the error page replaces the old same-origin child.
A parent whose load event waited for a parsing child receives LoadComplete after the frame's error page loads. A parent with a pending frame navigation keeps its readiness events unchanged.
In multiprocess mode, the frame's error page runs in a content process that differs from the host's, the parent's, and the failed process.

The child-site popup's own top-level document ran in the failed event loop. It still receives revocation before eight terminal callbacks, the exact reason, and a crash page, so one failure notifies several views. The parent-loop popup and an independent view keep their scope.

Late scripts, the held response tail, or a late navigation response reach no live document. After 300 milliseconds the parent keeps its identity and readiness, the frame keeps the same error page pipeline, and the engine reports no error.
Reload replaces the contained parent with a fresh identity, rejects the old scope, and loads the original child. A new URL recovers the parent and the child-site popup.
The same-site pending frame cases keep their earlier results, because the pending pipeline shares the parent's event loop and the parent's own document fails.
The contained view receives no engine notification of the frame's failure.

A first set of control runs was stopped after the fixture changed, so that a parent revocation inside the barrier is reported before the frame state check. limitations: Multiprocess evidence uses unsandboxed children on macOS arm64 with software rendering.
The contained view receives no engine notification of a frame's failure. The host cannot evaluate in a frame, so the fixture reads the frame's state through a probe.
A failed send to a frame's pipeline still enters Servo's send-error path, which replaces the whole view. No fixture checks that path.
No fixture checks a failed frame with a healthy pending navigation, a failed frame in an inactive parent document, or inactive history pipelines of a surviving view in the failed event loop.

History traversal inside a frame after a contained failure remains unchecked. A frame's initial navigation, a navigation that the child starts, and a pending traversal inside a frame remain unchecked.
A content security policy of the parent could block the frame's crash fetch. No fixture checks this.
Kills during JavaScript execution or IPC writes remain unchecked. Every kill happens at a barrier.
No new Linux, native-input, release-performance, or remote CI evidence is claimed.
